These are successful controller recordings, replayed from a fresh public `Game::start` by `tests/replay_validation.rs`. Each frame contains four controller masks; absent players have a zero mask. The fixture contains no positions, health overrides, enemy edits, or completion flags. The test requires the final input to complete its stage (or campaign). For each standalone stage recording it then sends 256 idle-input ticks and checks the next stage or ending, including preserved difficulty and player count. Standalone recordings are bounded at 36,000 ticks; continuous campaigns at 240,000 ticks.

`cargo run --example replay_matrix -- --validate-all` checks the existing recordings. Its success only covers those files. `cargo run --example replay_matrix` requires all 108 normal/hard stage and player-count combinations. `cargo run --example replay_matrix -- --campaign` requires eight continuous campaigns, carrying gameplay state between stages. Missing recordings and unsuccessful outcomes make the matrix commands fail.

`cargo run --example validate_playthrough -- --stage 0 --players 1 --output /tmp/route.json` searches legal inputs and independently replays a successful result before saving it. `--hard` selects hard mode. `--campaign --ticks 240000` searches a continuous campaign, carrying gameplay state through every stage transition. `--beam` and `--depth` tune lookahead; `--global` uses a best-first search. `--prefix FILE` replays an existing input prefix before continuing the search, preserving all campaign state. `--campaign --global --prefix FILE` searches a continuation of the current room and then resumes campaign planning. `--trace FILE` writes attempted inputs for debugging, including failures; these traces must not be placed here as completed fixtures.

The separate `../arena_entry_normal_stage02_player1.json` fixture verifies the boss entrance and scripted camera transition. It is a scenario recording, not a completed stage.

`cargo run --release --example splice_replays -- PREFIX ROUTE OUTPUT_TRACE` tries a recorded next-stage route after a legal campaign prefix. It can insert up to 255 idle frames before the preceding exit to search timing variations. Its output is a partial campaign trace for `--prefix`, not a completed-campaign fixture. All stage transitions and outcomes are simulated through controller inputs.

Planner controls include held-jump and release/rejump variants, charged shooting, and independent horizontal movement branches inside multiplayer boss arenas. `--waypoint X,Y` supplies a temporary navigation target, cleared after the controller reaches it; it does not move an actor directly. `--solo-climb` moves the highest living player during scrolling sections while teammates receive idle/fire inputs, then resumes cooperative arena control. These are search strategies only; the saved file records every controller independently and replays against unmodified gameplay.

`campaign-normal-players1.json` is a complete continuous normal campaign: 80,476 controller frames, all 13 stages, ending screen reached with score, health, equipment, remaining lives, and random state carried through the public stage-transition path. Other standalone recordings establish only their own stage outcomes and transitions; their presence does not imply a continuous campaign.

The regression corpus requires complete normal and hard solo campaigns, every distinct normal/hard boss stage in solo play, and the extra hard final boss with each player count. Deleting these recordings fails the test. The optional 108-case matrix remains a separate coverage target. `--nodes N` bounds global search; on exhaustion `--trace` retains its best legal partial continuation for a subsequent `--prefix` attempt. `--step N` controls the controller macro duration (1–60 ticks, default 6).

`campaign-hard-players1.json` completes the continuous hard campaign through all 14 stages and its ending in 77,249 controller frames. Both solo campaigns are required by the regression corpus.

A deterministic randomized escape search is available with `--random-trials N --random-ticks 1800 --step 18 --seed 34567`. It explores controller sequences for the current room, applies inputs only to living players, and preserves the best legal partial damage trace if no clear is found. It can be chained through `--prefix` or followed by regular campaign planning. A successful output still undergoes the same fresh independent replay.

`--ghost-support` enables an optional randomized-search controller for ghost teammates: approach the nearest unfrozen ordinary threat and pulse freeze shots, falling back to accompanying a living teammate. This supplies legal input only; it does not freeze actors directly.

`campaign-normal-players4.json` completes all 13 normal stages continuously with four independent controller slots in 49,835 ticks. It uses the public cooperative stage transitions, ghost states and shared lives, and is required by the regression corpus.

`campaign-hard-players4.json` completes all 14 hard stages continuously with four players in 53,019 ticks and is required by the regression corpus. Both hard campaigns include the recovered offscreen summoned-enemy cleanup behavior.
